Attila is, in my opinion, one of the best, if not the best, historical Total War titles out there: brutal, atmospheric, and full of replayability.

Yes, the performance optimization is bad and the campaign AI can feel overly hostile, with some frustrating mechanics (public order penalties, religion, loyalty).

But the depth of the factions, the unique cultural mechanics, and the sheer tension of its battles more than make up for it.

Every fight feels costly, every mistake you make might doom your campaign.

With the right overhaul mods (and there are many excellent ones), the game shines. If you're into challenge, grim late antiquity vibes, and meaningful campaigns, Attila is absolutely worth your time.

Despite playing 500 hours I'd say the game a) isn't challenging and b) has a game-ruining feature for me which hasn't been patched or modded. Towers collapse when you capture them. This seems a bit ridiculous to start with, like ancient barbarians had C4 to immediately destroy them, and because anyone within a radius to capture them will suffer heavy losses. I found this game-breaking when it happened in sieges, as you wouldn't be able to move your guys out the way by the time you captured the towers, so you would lose hundreds of men unnecessarily.

In terms of the challenge - it's just too easy even on harder difficulties as the WRE.

Oh and the battle maps completely lack variety. Forest, hills, open plain or river crossing are what you will see. No marshes/swamps, streams, patchworks of farms, ridges, broken/rocky terrain that might break up formations etc.

Total War Attila, souly in my opinion, is one of the greatest Total War games. It brings the enviorment into a critical position, in which you cannot just cross the desert without fatigute and heat sickness, or march your troops in the cold in England. It also brings in a warlike vibe. Instead of already formed kingdoms, you can form a empire playing as one of the migrating factions. Diplomacy is also a essential factor to the game, in which you cannot go unpunished for invading a nation that is friendly with several others. Highly recommend this game!

You built an empire beyond imagining.
A pinnacle of human achievement and the envy of the world.
Did you think it would last?

The eternal city.
That glorious monument to power culture and learning.
But the old wolf lies wounded by jackals and circled by vultures.
Worried to death by a thousand tiny, vicious mouths.
Brought low by your own arrogance!

These are the death-throws of Rome.
The light of civilisation gutters and dims.
And you've such precious time left to hide your women, for your children to cry.
Even at the moment of your final defeat you will take no comfort in oblivion...

For I am coming for you.

I RIDE WITH A MILLION WARRIORS!
I BRING THE END OF DAYS!
I AM THE SCOURGE OF GOD!

And I will watch your world burn...

I love the total war series. I really do, I have played them all. This one is Rome 2 with new challenges. These challenges were made to simulate real problems facing the world at this point, and to be honest, the way they are depicted in this game is very annoying. Asia and europe will be a wasteland by the time you get there, burned to the ground by marauding hordes. As long as Attilla is alive, hordes magically sprout from the ground in Crimea. Corruption is rampant and crippling. the economy is very hard to manage, and the farmland returns diminish as the game progresses. Dont get me wrong, Ive figured the way they want me to combat these problems. I just find them annoying and would rather not deal with them. These are not fun additions.

Honestly I love this game. I only have 89 hours of play time, but it would be more. Sadly, the reason for that is its hard to play this game with all the game crashing bugs. Rome 2 and Shogun 2 have been my favorites so far, but Attila would surpass them if the game would just run. If its not crashing from trying to open the family/politics tab because there are too many characters or from just crashing ending your turn, then this game would easily have over 1k hours from me since I got it last year. I just now uninstalled to try and redownload because the cut scene is choppy now and freezes, then the game itself does the same. I then tried to play Rome 2 and was laggy. Could be a problem on my end for that, not sure. The game crashing bugs however are not my fault. I honestly wish Creative Assembly would get back to their old mindset of caring, and get their act together to fix old games. Hell even create new ones that are good, unlike Pharoah. The game was fun when it did work, but unfortunately its becoming more work than its worth to try and get it to work. Take this as a warning, buy or don't buy. Completely up to you as the consumer, I'm just here to warn about the bugs.

I heard a lot of hate going into this game, but its plain and simple, some classic Total War. I really enjoy the challenge of dealing with all these evil roaming hordes. It makes fighting on different fronts much more challenging. You never know where Attila and his horde will show up and raze your cities to the ground. Especially if you're taking cities that don't belong to your faction. You could invest so much into a city and then watch it all burn. It really makes you feel the loss and revenge threfore is so much sweeter. If you like previous total war games, its great. If you've never tried total war before, its as good a place to start as any other. Fantastic RTS.
